'''Tan Eng Chye''' ({{lang-zh|c=|p=Chén Yǒngcái|s=陈永财|t=陳永財}}) is a Singaporean mathematician and [[college administrator|university administrator]] who has been serving as the fifth president of the [[National University of Singapore]] since 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.nus.edu.Sg/highlights/prof-tan-eng-chye-be-next-nus-president|title=Prof Tan Eng Chye to be next NUS President|work=news.nus.com}}</ref> Prior to his presidency, he served as the deputy president of academic affairs and [[Provost (education)|provost]] at the National University of Singapore.

==Education==

Tan attended [[Raffles Institution]] between 1974 and 1979 before graduating from the [[National University of Singapore]] in 1985 with a [[Bachelor of Science]] (First Class Honours) degree in [[mathematics]]. He later went on to obtain his [[PhD]] from [[Yale University]] in 1989, under the guidance of [[Roger Evans Howe|Roger Howe]].<ref name="thesis-tan-1989">{{cite thesis |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/303762745/ |title=On some geometrical properties of K-types of representations |date=1989 |publisher=[[Yale University]] |type=Ph.D. |last=Tan |first=Eng-Chye |id={{ProQuest|303762745}} |url-access=subscription |oclc=54174603}}</ref>

==Career==
{{BLP sources section|date=August 2021}}
He joined NUS as a faculty member in the Department of Mathematics in 1985, as a Senior Tutor. In June 2003, he was appointed [[Dean (education)|Dean]] of the [[Faculty of Science, National University of Singapore|Faculty of Science]], a post he held till March 2007. Up till 2017, he served as NUS' Deputy President (Academic Affairs) and [[Provost (education)|Provost]].

Tan Eng Chye's research interests are [[Representation of a Lie group|representation theory of Lie groups]] and [[Lie algebra]]s, [[invariant theory]] and [[algebraic combinatorics]]. In collaboration with [[Roger Evans Howe|Roger Howe]], he has written a graduate-level textbook on non-Abelian [[harmonic analysis]] which was described in a review as "Every chapter is full of beautiful mathematics that is not as well known as it deserves to be."<ref>{{cite web|url=
https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1993-28-01/S0273-0979-1993-00345-8/S0273-0979-1993-00345-8.pdf|title=Bulletin of the American mathematical Society, Book Reviews|publisher=American Mathematical Society}}</ref> He has also been active in promoting mathematics, having established the Singapore Mathematical Society Enrichment Programmes in 1994, revamped the [[Singapore Mathematical Olympiad]] in 1995 to allow more participation from students, and initiated a series of project teaching workshops for teachers in 1998. He served as president of the [[Singapore Mathematical Society]] from 2001 to 2005 and President of the South East Asian Mathematical Society from 2004 to 2005.

=== 2018–present: NUS presidency ===
On 28 July 2017, Tan was named as the next president of NUS, taking over [[Tan Chorh Chuan]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Davie|first=Sandra|date=28 July 2017|title=NUS provost Tan Eng Chye will take over as university's president next year|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/education/nus-provost-tan-eng-chye-will-take-over-as-nus-president-next-year|access-date=9 September 2021|website=The Straits Times}}</ref> He assumed office at the start of 2018. Along with the appointed, he was appointed to [[A*STAR]]'s board as well, taking the seat meant for the university's president.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Williams|first=Ann|date=29 December 2017|title=New NUS, NTU presidents among 3 new board members for A*Star in 2018|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/business/economy/new-nus-ntu-presidents-among-3-new-board-members-for-astar-in-2018|access-date=9 September 2021|website=The Straits Times|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210909221330/https://www.straitstimes.com/business/economy/new-nus-ntu-presidents-among-3-new-board-members-for-astar-in-2018|archive-date=9 September 2021|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2020, NUS raised US$300 million through its first green bond.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Tay|first=Vivienne|date=27 May 2020|title=NUS raises S$300m in its first green bond issuance|url=https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/banking-finance/nus-raises-s300m-in-its-first-green-bond-issuance|access-date=9 September 2021|website=www.businesstimes.com.sg}}</ref> In the same year, it established a research institute called the Asian Institute of Digital Finance along with the [[Monetary Authority of Singapore]] and [[National Research Foundation (Singapore)|National Research Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Tan|first=Sue-Ann|date=4 August 2020|title=Singapore to set up Asian digital finance research institute by end-2020|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/business/singapore-to-set-up-asian-digital-finance-research-institute-by-end-2020|access-date=9 September 2021|website=The Straits Times}}</ref>

In 2020, Tan said in an interview that he had plans for NUS to "tear down structures that inhibit interdisciplinarity",<ref>{{Cite web|title=COVID-19 starts push for more interdisciplinary research|url=https://www.universityworldnews.com/post.php?story=20200724125405567|access-date=9 September 2021|website=University World News}}</ref> with Professor [[Joanne Roberts]] of [[Yale-NUS College]] commenting that there were similarities between Yale-NUS and Tan's plans.<ref>{{Cite web|title=NUS' big push for interdisciplinary learning: Timely change but there'll be practical challenges, experts say|url=https://www.todayonline.com/singapore/big-push-interdisciplinary-learning-nus-timely-change-therell-be-practical-challenges|access-date=9 September 2021|website=TODAYonline}}</ref> On 22 September 2020, NUS unveiled its plans for an interdisciplinary college, the College of Humanities and Sciences, allowing students to take courses from both the Faculty of Science and the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web|title=NUS unveils draft plans to set up combined College of Humanities and Sciences in 2021|url=https://www.todayonline.com/singapore/nus-unveils-draft-plans-set-combined-college-humanities-and-sciences-2021|access-date=9 September 2021|website=TODAYonline}}</ref> The new college took in its first intake in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Common modules, various subject combinations for first cohort at new NUS College of Humanities and Sciences in 2021|url=https://www.todayonline.com/singapore/common-modules-various-subject-combinations-first-cohort-new-nus-college-humanities-and|access-date=9 September 2021|website=TODAYonline}}</ref>

As part of a broader plan to introduce interdisciplinary colleges, in 2021,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Wei Kai|first=Ng|date=13 September 2021|title=Yale-NUS closure part of NUS interdisciplinary road map, cost not the main motivation: Chan Chun Sing|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/parenting-education/yale-nus-closure-part-of-nus-interdisciplinary-road-map-cost-not-the|access-date=13 September 2021|website=The Straits Times}}</ref> Tan announced that Yale-NUS College would be closed by 2025, with 2021 intake of freshmen being the last intake. The college would also be merged with NUS' University Scholars Programme to offer a new curriculum. The decision was unilaterally made by NUS, and came as a surprise to Yale-NUS' students and faculty, NUS' faculty, and Yale.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Students, faculty angry over closure of Yale-NUS College|url=https://www.universityworldnews.com/post.php?story=20210901095937911|access-date=9 September 2021|website=University World News}}</ref> More than 10,000 people had signed a petition calling for the reversal of the decision.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Wei Kai|first1=Ng|last2=Wing|first2=Ang|date=31 August 2021|title=Over 10,000 sign petition calling for reversal of Yale-NUS merger, students and alumni seek answers at townhall|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/parenting-education/over-9500-sign-petition-calling-on-nus-to-reverse-merger-decision-on|access-date=9 September 2021|website=The Straits Times}}</ref> Questions about the decision filed in the [[Singapore Parliament]] by various members of parliament were answered on 13 September 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=WP MPs to file parliamentary questions on Yale-NUS, USP merger for possible debate at Sept 13 sitting|url=https://www.todayonline.com/singapore/wp-mps-file-parliamentary-questions-yale-nus-usp-merger-possible-debate-sept-13-sitting|access-date=9 September 2021|website=TODAYonline}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

== Honours and awards ==
Tan received the [[Pingat Pentadbiran Awam|Pingat Pentadbiran Awam, Emas]] (Public Administration Medal, Gold) in Singapore's National Day Awards 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Singapore|first=Prime Minister's Office|date=17 November 2018|title=PMO &#124; Recipients|url=http://www.pmo.gov.sg/National-Day-Awards/Recipients|website=Prime Minister's Office Singapore}}</ref> He has been a Fellow of the Singapore National Academy of Science since 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nine NUS professors conferred prestigious SNAS Fellowships|url=http://news.nus.edu.sg/highlights/343-nine-nus-professors-conferred-prestigious-snas-fellowships|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161118165947/http://news.nus.edu.sg/highlights/343-nine-nus-professors-conferred-prestigious-snas-fellowships|archive-date=18 November 2016}}</ref> He was conferred the Wilbur Lucius Cross Medal by the Yale Graduate School Alumni Association in 2018,<ref>{{cite web|title=NUS President conferred Yale medal|url=http://news.nus.edu.sg/highlights/nus-president-conferred-yale-medal|work=news.nus.com}}</ref> and received an Honorary Doctor of Science from the University of Southampton, UK in the same year.<ref>{{cite web|title=NUS President receives honorary degree from Southampton|url=http://news.nus.edu.sg/highlights/nus-president-receives-honorary-degree-southampton|work=news.nus.com}}</ref>

Tan was conferred the title of Knight of the [[Legion of Honour|French Order of the Legion of Honour]] on 5 July 2022, in recognition of his distinguished contributions in education and research.<ref>{{Cite web|title=NUS President Prof Tan Eng Chye conferred Knight of the French Order of the Legion of Honour|url=https://news.nus.edu.sg/nus-president-prof-tan-eng-chye-conferred-knight-of-the-french-order-of-the-legion-of-honour/|work=news.nus.com}}</ref>
